events.title: Flask web framework released
events.summary: Armin Ronacher released Flask on April 1, 2010 — a microframework for Python web apps built on Werkzeug and Jinja2.
events.about: Flask gives you routing, templates, and sessions without Django's batteries — you pick your own ORM and auth. Used for microservices, internal tools, ML model APIs, and prototypes. Example: a 50-line app that serves JSON from a SQLite DB and renders HTML with Jinja templates.

narrative.whyChosen: Flask became Python's lightweight alternative to Django for APIs and small services.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved a microframework could stay minimal while powering serious production apps via extensions.
narrative.problemSolved: Django was heavy for tiny APIs; developers wanted WSGI routing and templates without full MVC ceremony.

sources.title: Ronacher — April 1st Post Mortem (Flask release, April 1, 2010)

events.title: F# 2.0 shipped with Visual Studio 2010
events.summary: On April 12, 2010, Microsoft shipped F# 2.0 with Visual Studio 2010 — a functional-first language for .NET, ready for production teams.
events.about: F# combines functional programming (immutable data, pattern matching) with full access to .NET libraries. Used in quantitative finance, data science, and Azure services. Several features Don Syme pioneered in F# later appeared in C#, including LINQ-style data queries and async/await.

narrative.whyChosen: F# brought industrial-strength functional programming into Visual Studio alongside C# and VB.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved functional programming could ship in enterprise tooling, not just research prototypes.
narrative.problemSolved: Functional languages lacked .NET libraries and enterprise IDE support; researchers needed a practical FP on Microsoft's platform.

sources.title: Microsoft Research — The early history of F# (productization 2007–10, F# 2.0)

events.title: .NET 4.0 and C# 4.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET Framework 4.0 on April 12, 2010 with C# 4.0 dynamic typing, optional parameters, and `async` preparation via the Task Parallel Library.
events.about: C# 4's `dynamic` keyword made COM and Office automation less painful; optional and named arguments cleaned up APIs. The Task Parallel Library laid groundwork for `async`/`await in C# 5 — keeping .NET competitive for Windows desktop and server through the 2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 4 added dynamic interop and TPL — stepping stones to modern async .NET.
narrative.whyImportant: Dynamic typing bridged C# and scripting/COM worlds without abandoning static safety elsewhere.
narrative.problemSolved: Office and legacy COM APIs were painful to call from strongly typed C#.
